entities.summary: Cyril of Jerusalem (b. 313 CE, Jerusalem) was a bishop of the Eastern Orthodox Church, known for his theological writings and role in the Council of Jerusalem (385 CE), which addressed the Gentile mission and the inclusion of non-Jews in the Church. As Patriarch of Jerusalem, he promoted unity and cooperation between Orthodox Christians and other Christian denominations, influencing the development of Christian theology and ecclesiastical governance. Cyril's writings, particularly the Catechism of Cyril, remain significant in the Eastern Orthodox tradition, providing insights into the nature of Christ and the relationship between the Church and the world. His legacy continues to shape the spiritual practices and theological debates of the Orthodox Church, making him a crucial figure in the history of Christianity.
